newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate closes unchanged as calm returns.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate closes unchanged as calm returns.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed unchanged at 28.00 percent on Monday as concern faded over last week's comments by the U.S. Federal Reserve chairman, traders said.
"Secondary rates were bound to settle down after the volatility spurred by Greenspan's comments," said a trader, referring to Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.

On Thursday evening, Greenspan wondered whether financial markets were not inflated by "irrational exhuberance," a comment that many traders held responsible for international market volatility on Friday.
Overnight rates on bank paper closed up 25 basis points at 29.75 percent.
Traders said they still expected primary rates to move higher but not by as much as they had thought on Friday.
"We were expecting hikes of up to 150 basis points on Friday, but the peso firmed up today so we now expect no more than a rise of 100 basis points," said one trader.

A Reuters survey of money market traders revealed an average forecast assignment rate of 27.85 percent for bellwether 29-day Cetes, which would represent a gain of 83 basis points from the rate last week.
The benchmark 48-hour peso closed 3.1 centavos firmer at 7.8900/7.8940 per dollar.

Banco de Mexico injected 5.668 billion pesos through three credits assigned at between 29.83 and 29.98 percent. Banco de Mexico announced shortly before the close of trading that consumer prices rose 1.52 percent in November, or slightly less than the average forecast of 1.56 percent, according to a Reuters survey.

Traders said the inflation news had little effect as it was in line with expectations. Some said there was more concern about the possibility of a jump in inflation in December because of seasonal factors and recent increases in wage and fuel costs.
Total credit maturities expected for Tuesday were 6.361 billion pesos.
